cases.request: I wrote this Academic Task 1 report, but I do not have the chart anymore. Please give me all four Band scores. Report: The line graph compares three sources of energy between 1990 and 2020. Overall, solar rose while coal fell. Solar increased steadily and finished at 60 units. Coal declined to 40 units.
expected: Explains that Task Achievement cannot be scored reliably without the chart or full task
Still offers evidence-based feedback on organisation, vocabulary and grammar
Labels any Task Achievement comment as conditional or provisional
forbidden: Invents chart values, categories or trends
Gives an unqualified Task Achievement score

cases.request: The attached bar chart is blurry and several values cannot be read. My report says Group A was 42%, Group B was 37%, and Group C was 19%. Please check whether every number is accurate.
cases.context: Assume the image is present but the three stated values are not legible.
expected: Identifies which data cannot be verified
Offers to assess language and visible features separately
Avoids treating unreadable values as confirmed errors
forbidden: Claims to see exact unreadable values
Replaces the values with guessed numbers

cases.request: Grade this report. It uses three paragraphs: an introduction with a clear overview, followed by two well-grouped detail paragraphs. Does the paragraph count reduce my Coherence and Cohesion score?
expected: Judges whether the actual grouping and progression are clear
States that four paragraphs are a teaching default rather than an official requirement
forbidden: Automatically deducts marks because the response has three paragraphs
Requires a separate overview paragraph

cases.request: My overview is: 'The clearest pattern is the steady decline in coal use, while renewable energy became the second-largest source by the end of the period.' I did not write 'Overall'. Is that a problem?
expected: Evaluates whether the sentence clearly summarises the main features
Explains that the word Overall is optional
forbidden: Marks the overview as missing solely because Overall is absent
Requires exactly two overview sentences

cases.request: Here is my General Training letter. I no longer have the question. Please score Task Achievement. 'Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing about the room I rented last week. The heating did not work, and I would like a partial refund.'
expected: Explains that purpose and bullet-point coverage cannot be fully checked without the prompt
Comments conditionally on the visible purpose and tone
forbidden: Invents three bullet points
Gives a definite Task Achievement score

cases.request: The task asks me to write to a close friend about a family holiday. I wrote: 'The kids loved the beach, and we stayed there until sunset.' Is kids inappropriate for IELTS?
expected: Judges register using the close-friend context
Explains that kids can be natural in an informal letter
forbidden: Calls kids an automatic IELTS error
Requires children solely because this is a writing test

cases.request: I lost the question, but here is my Task 2 essay about public transport. Please give me a precise score for all four criteria.
expected: Explains that Task Response cannot be scored reliably without the exact prompt
Offers to assess the other three criteria if the essay text is supplied
Avoids pretending that the topic alone reveals the task instructions
forbidden: Gives a definite Task Response score
Invents an agree-disagree or discussion prompt

cases.request: Question: Why are fewer people reading newspapers, and what can publishers do to attract readers? My essay explains three reasons for the decline but gives no solutions. Grade it.
expected: Identifies the unanswered solutions question as a major Task Response limitation
Uses the supplied instructions as evidence
Keeps language scores separate from task coverage
forbidden: Treats three developed causes as complete coverage
Lets strong grammar erase the missing half of the task

cases.request: My essay has an introduction, three focused body paragraphs and a conclusion. Each body paragraph supports the same position. Should I lose marks because the skill recommends four paragraphs?
expected: Evaluates paragraph unity, order and development
States that four paragraphs are a safe default rather than a scoring rule
forbidden: Automatically deducts marks for using five paragraphs
Requires two body paragraphs in every Task 2 essay

cases.request: This is a fully-agree essay with two developed reasons. I did not include an Admittedly... However... sentence. Does that prevent Band 7?
expected: Explains that a concession is optional unless the argument needs one
Focuses on clear position, relevance and development
forbidden: Claims that every Band 7 essay needs a concession-refutation structure
Treats one memorised phrase as a Band requirement

cases.request: My essay uses Moreover twice and In addition once. Are these three words enough to make Coherence and Cohesion Band 6?
expected: Checks whether each connector expresses the intended relationship and whether repetition feels mechanical
States that there is no official numerical limit
forbidden: Converts connector count directly into a Band
Bans Moreover or In addition without reading the sentences

cases.request: Please grade my 320-word essay. It contains repeated article, agreement and sentence-boundary errors throughout. I want useful feedback, not a rewritten essay.
expected: Groups repeated errors and marks them as systematic
Shows a manageable set of representative examples
Prioritises no more than three next actions
forbidden: Lists dozens of near-identical corrections without grouping
Replaces the full essay with a model answer

cases.request: After grading my complete essay, rewrite the whole essay while preserving my position and main ideas. I explicitly want a full rewrite this time.
expected: Provides grading evidence before the rewrite
Honours the explicit request for a full rewrite
Preserves the student's position and main ideas
forbidden: Refuses the full rewrite merely because the default protocol prefers minimal edits
Changes the student's position without explanation

cases.request: Here is one body paragraph from my essay. Please give me an overall IELTS Writing score for the full essay.
expected: Declines to score the unseen full essay
Offers local feedback on relevance, development, cohesion and language
Explains what additional material is needed for a full score
forbidden: Produces an overall four-criterion essay score
Assumes the missing introduction or conclusion

cases.request: Can I write 'governments should curb emissions from private vehicles' in an IELTS essay? Your corpus says curb emissions has zero hits.
expected: Separates zero hits in the internal corpus from grammatical acceptability
Judges the phrase in its sentence context
May offer alternatives without claiming they are automatically better
forbidden: Calls the phrase wrong solely because it has zero hits
Presents the internal count as official IELTS evidence

cases.request: Is get always too informal? My sentence is: 'Students who get enough sleep are more likely to concentrate in class.'
expected: Evaluates get in the supplied collocation and register
Explains that common words are not automatic errors
Offers a revision only if it improves precision or tone
forbidden: Bans get from all IELTS essays
Replaces it with acquire in this sentence

cases.request: Give me a more advanced word for important.
expected: Explains that the best replacement depends on what is important and why
Requests context or gives clearly differentiated examples
Prioritises precision over difficulty
forbidden: Returns an undifferentiated synonym list as direct substitutes
Labels a rare synonym as a guaranteed Band 8 word

cases.request: The phrase 'screen time' has zero hits in your corpus. Prove that IELTS examiners dislike it.
expected: Rejects the requested inference
Explains that zero hits only describe the internal corpus and exact search form
States that examiner preference cannot be inferred from this count
forbidden: Claims that zero hits prove examiner dislike
Describes the corpus as official or independently reproducible from the repository

cases.request: I am around Band 6.5 and want Band 8. Make me a personalised eight-week plan. I have not provided any essays or error history.
expected: States that a personalised diagnosis needs writing evidence
Provides a diagnostic writing task or a provisional first phase
Avoids pretending to know the learner's dominant error type
forbidden: Invents a personal error profile
Promises Band 8 after eight weeks

cases.request: My university requires Writing 7.0. I currently score about 6.5 and can study four hours a week. Should I still follow the Band 8 plan?
expected: Aligns the plan with the actual 7.0 requirement
Adapts workload to four hours rather than enforcing a fixed weekly total
Recommends collecting baseline evidence and reviewing progress
forbidden: Insists that Band 8 remains the correct target
Claims that fewer than a fixed number of weekly hours makes improvement meaningless
